newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-SCHALKE TRIUMPH OVER TENERIFE TO MAKE HISTORY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SCHALKE TRIUMPH OVER TENERIFE TO MAKE HISTORY.

text.p: Schalke of Germany scored a thrilling 2-0 extra-time victory over Spanish side Tenerife in the second leg of their UEFA Cup semifinal on Tuesday.
Headed goals from Thomas Linke and Marc Wilmots gave Schalke a 2-1 aggregate win which sent them into the first European final in their 93-year history.

Bidding to overcome a 1-0 deficit from the first leg but deprived of first-choice strikers Youri Mulder and Martin Max through injury, Schalke began cautiously but grew in confidence as the game went on.
Schalke, who take their name from a district of their home city of Gelsenkirchen, went close through Czech international Jiri Nemec and Ingo Anderbruegge in the first half.
The German side looked particularly dangerous from set-pieces, with former Germany star Olaf Thon flighting in several inviting free-kicks and corners.
Linke rose above the Tenerife defence in the 68th minute to head a Thon corner past the Spanish side's Swedish goalkeeper Beng Andersson.
The defender's goal levelled the aggregate score at 1-1 and proved enough to take the tie into extra time.
Thon was again the provider in the 17th minute of extra time, sending in a free-kick for Wilmots to convert.
The Gelsenkirchen team -- cheered on by more than 55,000 fans in their Park Stadium -- deserved the win having shown more invention and applying more pressure.
"I said all along that we might need 120 minutes," Schalke coach Huub Stevens said. "We had to keep calm and know that we had more experience and that we were fitter than Tenerife."

Tenerife's German coach Juup Heynckes congratulated Schalke on their victory and said his own side -- also bidding to reach their first ever European final -- had achieved a great deal simply by reaching this stage of the competition.
"Schalke deserved to win," said Heynckes, who was deprived of several key players through suspension. "They exploited their strength in set pieces."
Linke, who also scored along with Wilmots in Schalke's quarter-final win over Valencia, was delighted with the victory.
"Even if we hadn't gone through, we've still been sensational in the UEFA Cup this season," he said.
Tuesday's tie was only Schalke's second ever European semifinal. They went out to England's Manchester City in the 1970 European Cup Winners' Cup.
Stevens said he had not yet begun to think about Internazionale of Milan, Schalke's opponents in the final. They beat Monaco in the other semifinal.
"We wanted to get into the final, we've done it and we're very happy," said the Dutch coach who came to Schalke earlier in the season.
